body:
I believe this is a documentation issue. I don't *quite* understand all the details well enough to fully explain them, but there are differences in the internal coordinate spaces of the Compatibility and the Forward+/Mobile renderers that won't be changed for compatibility reasons. One of those differences is the z value of the far clip plane. https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10273 gets into it a little.

In 4.4 we now have access to `CLIP_SPACE_FAR` (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/95057) and preprocessor defines (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/98549), so you now have the tools to write shaders that will work in all renderers.

In this case, if the comment is accurate and the goal is to always render at the far clip plane, you might be able to use:
`POSITION.z = CLIP_SPACE_FAR;`

I think that the existing docs issue https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs/issues/10204 in theory covers this case. But we should probably leave this issue open, to track specifically documenting the far clip z value.

Thank you for the addition.

I'm not the author of the original shader so I can't comment about the accuracy of the comment.

All I can say is that `POSITION.z = CLIP_SPACE_FAR;` unfortunately does not fix the issue (the background stars still render on top of the object and the wanted effect is that they render behind it).
